ai.title: Update CLI menu prompt examples
ai.summary: Replaced 'Refactor a large file into smaller files' with 'Refactor a component into multiple components' in the CLI menu examples. Adjusts suggested prompts to better align with component-based refactoring patterns. Change applies only to npm-app/src/menu.ts.

eli5.text: The list of example tasks the assistant shows you in its menu now suggests breaking a large piece of code into multiple smaller pieces, instead of suggesting splitting one big file into smaller files. If you open the menu, you will see this wording change; it only affects what examples are displayed, not how the assistant actually works. This change is live today and applies to anyone using the command-line version of the tool.

ai.title: Reduce buffer size in process-stream.ts
ai.summary: Decreased `bufferSize` from 250 to 50 in `backend/src/process-stream.ts`. This change affects the streaming tag processing logic. The smaller buffer size is intended for demo purposes.

eli5.text: When the assistant streams a response token by token, it now collects the text in much smaller batches, about eight times less at a time, before sending each batch. You would only notice this if you were specifically watching how quickly small pieces of text arrive during a streamed reply; otherwise, the difference is invisible. The change is live today and is part of a set of adjustments made for demonstration purposes.

ai.title: Stop duplicating previous changes in websocket responses
ai.summary: Removed concatenation of `previousChanges` and `changes` in `backend/src/websockets/websocket-action.ts`. `previousChanges` were being applied twice during user input processing. Responses now send only the current `changes` array for both `toolCall` and `response-complete` actions.

eli5.text: When the assistant processes your input, it was accidentally including a list of recent actions twice in its replies, which could cause duplicate or repeated suggestions to appear for you. The system now sends each list only once, so replies no longer repeat prior steps. If you looked, you'd see cleaner, less redundant responses without the same details duplicated within a single message.

ai.title: Implement API limits for anon, free, and paid users
ai.summary: New `QuotaManager` and `MessageCostTracker` enforce tiered usage limits (1k anon, 2.5k free, 50k paid) via `common/src/constants.ts`. `message-cost-tracker.ts` calculates credits using model-specific token rates plus 20% profit margin, replacing legacy `billing/message.ts`. Integration touches `authentication.knowledge.md` for session quota application and `web/src/app/pricing/page.tsx` for UI updates.

eli5.text: Starting today, the system that runs in the background now keeps track of how much you're using it, and it applies different limits depending on whether you're signed in, have a free account, or pay for a subscription. If you're just visiting without an account, you can use it up to a point before being asked to sign up or log in; if you have a free account, you get a bit more; and if you're a paying subscriber, you get a much higher allowance. When the system checks your usage, it now also factors in the cost of the specific features you're using, with a small built-in margin added on top, so heavier tasks count for more against your limit. Anonymous visitors who exceed their cap will be prompted to authenticate to keep going.

ai.title: Bump version to 1.0.80
ai.summary: Package version updated from 1.0.79 to 1.0.80 in `npm-app/package.json`. Internal release increment.

eli5.text: If you update the assistant to the latest version, you will get a package that includes fixes and new usage limits rolled up together. The public-facing change in this release is that anonymous, free, and paying users now have different tiered limits on how much they can use the assistant at once. You would notice this only when you install or update from an app store, since the version label itself is just a behind-the-scenes number used for tracking releases.
